name: 10 Degree Channel (10° N)
separates: Little Andaman (Andaman Islands) from Car Nicobar (Nicobar Islands)
significance: Major international maritime waterway ~150 km wide separating the Andaman group from the Nicobar group in the Bay of Bengal.
examFacts: UPSC CSE Classic Question: Exactly 10° N latitude passes through this waterway separating the Andaman Islands (Little Andaman) from the Nicobar Islands (Car Nicobar).
Depth ranges from 730 m to over 1,000 m, making it a safe navigational route for international merchant vessels into the Malacca Strait.
Monitored round the clock by the Andaman and Nicobar Command (ANC) based at Port Blair.

name: 9 Degree Channel (9° N)
separates: Minicoy Island from the main Lakshadweep archipelago (Kalpeni and Suheli Par)
significance: Strategically vital ~200 km wide shipping lane in the Arabian Sea through which almost all merchant transit between Europe/Middle East and Southeast Asia passes.
examFacts: Separates Minicoy Island in the south from the northern islands of Lakshadweep (specifically Kalpeni and Suheli).
One of the busiest commercial sea corridors in the Indian Ocean carrying over 80,000 ships annually.
Heavily patrolled by the Indian Navy and Indian Coast Guard from INS Dweeprakshak (Kavaratti).

name: 8 Degree Channel (8° N)
separates: Minicoy Island (India) from the Maldives (Ihavandhippolhu Atoll)
significance: International maritime boundary line (IMBL) separating the Republic of India from the Republic of Maldives.
examFacts: Marks the maritime border between India's southernmost territory in Lakshadweep (Minicoy Island) and the northernmost atoll of Maldives.
Maritime boundary formalized under the 1976 Indo-Maldives Maritime Agreement.
Direct western approach to the vital Indian Ocean shipping lanes.

name: Duncan Passage
separates: Rutland Island (South Andaman) from Little Andaman
significance: A 48 km wide strait in the Bay of Bengal lying between South Andaman and Little Andaman.
examFacts: UPSC CSE Classic Question: Duncan Passage lies between South Andaman (specifically Rutland Island) and Little Andaman.
Contains small islet stepping stones including The Sisters and The Brothers islands.
Acts as an inner passage for coastal shipping across the Andaman archipelago.

name: Great Channel (Six Degree Channel / 6° N)
separates: Great Nicobar (Indira Point, India) from Sumatra Island (Aceh Province, Indonesia)
significance: Strategic choke point guarding the western entrance to the Malacca Strait; vital to India's 'Act East' policy and maritime security.
examFacts: Also known as the Six Degree Channel because the international maritime boundary runs near 6° N latitude.
Indira Point (6°45' N), India's southernmost geographical point, directly overlooks this channel.
The Indian Government's flagship Great Nicobar Mega-Project envisions an International Container Transshipment Terminal (ICTT) at Galathea Bay on this channel.

name: Palk Strait & Adam's Bridge (Ram Setu)
separates: Tamil Nadu (India) from the Jaffna Peninsula (Northern Province, Sri Lanka)
significance: Inlet of the Bay of Bengal separating southeastern India from Sri Lanka, bounded in the south by Pamban Island and Adam's Bridge shoal chain.
examFacts: Named after Robert Palk, Governor of Madras Presidency during the East India Company period (1755-67).
The shallow chain of limestone shoals between Pamban Island (Dhanushkodi, India) and Mannar Island (Sri Lanka) is known as Adam's Bridge or Ram Setu.
Drained by the Vaigai River from Tamil Nadu.
Site of the controversial Sethusamudram Shipping Canal Project proposal.

name: Gulf of Mannar
separates: Southeastern tip of India (Coromandel Coast / Tuticorin) from Western Sri Lanka
significance: Shallow bay forming part of the Laccadive Sea; designated as India's first Marine Biosphere Reserve (1989).
examFacts: First Marine Biosphere Reserve in South and Southeast Asia, encompassing 21 uninhabited islands and rich coral reefs.
Home to the vulnerable Dugong (Sea Cow), India's premier marine mammal, and endangered Olive Ridley sea turtles.
Historically famous for natural pearl oyster fisheries celebrated since the Sangam era (Korkai port of Pandyan kingdom).
